audit_scope.description: This batch covers EVM recursion limits (ethereum __init__), EL block size validation (EIP-7934), P2P data availability protocol (EIP-7801 etha), EL cold/warm access gas repricing (EIP-2929), EL PUSH0 opcode (EIP-3855), cryptographic hash primitives (keccak256/512), EL transaction gas cap (EIP-7825), Ethash PoW verification, EL contract creation storage validation (EIP-7610), and Cancun block instruction opcodes.

out_of_scope: Full EVM opcode set beyond block/push/storage
Full consensus state machine beyond block propagation

el_vectors.threat: Submit transactions with excessive gas limits, craft CREATE2 targeting residual storage addresses, deploy contracts exceeding block size limits
Send oversized blocks exceeding 8 MiB RLP limit, false data availability bitmask advertising, eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks
Exploit cold access gas costs for DoS, stack overflow via deep recursion, manipulate PREVRANDAO-dependent logic

cl_vectors.threat: Construct blocks with malicious environmental data (manipulated timestamps, coinbase), include transactions exceeding gas cap, produce oversized blocks
False data availability claims via etha bitmask, provide incorrect PoW verification data

misclassified_entities.reason: Hash function caller (keccak256) is an internal component (transaction validation, state root computation), not an external entity sending data into the system from outside.
Hash512 function caller is an internal component (Ethash protocol), not an external entity.
Light client performing local PoW verification using hashimoto_light is an internal verification mode, not an external entity sending data into the system.
Application layer requesting historical data in EIP-7801 is an internal component (higher-level application within the node), not an external entity.
Duplicate - beacon chain in Cancun block instructions is the same as CL via Engine API already modeled. PREVRANDAO source is provided through the block header from CL.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P devp2p / etha subprotocol (block propagation, data retrieval, handshake)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks and historical data over unauthenticated P2P network. May send oversized blocks, false availability bitmasks, or invalid data. All received data must be fully validated.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via JSON-RPC or P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction senders submit transactions with arbitrary gas limits and deployment targets. Gas cap (16,777,216) and contract creation collision/storage checks are required validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Untrusted Data Source via Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any data from network peers or user transactions is untrusted input that passes through keccak hash functions for integrity verification. Hash function security is foundational.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P block propagation (block headers with PoW/environmental data)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers set block environmental data (coinbase, timestamp, PREVRANDAO) and submit PoW solutions. Timestamp manipulation within protocol bounds is possible. All block data requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Creator via CREATE/CREATE2
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can attempt contract creation. EIP-7610 adds storage emptiness check to EIP-684's nonce/code checks. Must validate target address has zero nonce, zero code, AND empty storage.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P devp2p (oversized blocks, false handshake data)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker nodes may craft blocks exceeding MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) or transactions exceeding gas cap to cause resource exhaustion. Early size validation is critical.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Block RLP-encoded size must be validated against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) before expensive processing. Handshake must validate networkId, genesis hash, and forkId. Data availability bitmask claims must not be trusted without verification.

Transaction gasLimit must be validated against cap of 16,777,216 (2^24) at both mempool acceptance and block validation. Contract creation transactions must pass EIP-684 + EIP-7610 collision/storage checks.

Hash functions accept arbitrary byte inputs. Security relies on Keccak collision resistance and preimage resistance. Hash output is trusted as deterministic identifier of input. All client implementations must produce identical results.

Block environmental data (timestamp, coinbase, PREVRANDAO) is set by block proposer within protocol constraints. PREVRANDAO should not be treated as secure randomness. Timestamp manipulation within ~15 second bounds is possible. For historical PoW: Ethash verification required (hash <= target difficulty).

Three-way validation required: (1) target nonce == 0, (2) target code length == 0, (3) target storage is empty (EIP-7610 addition). Failure triggers revert as invalid opcode. This prevents code overwriting and residual storage exploitation for all 28 known mainnet addresses with pre-EIP-161 residual storage.

Size check must occur early in validation pipeline before expensive operations (signature verification, state transition). MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) provides 2 MiB safety margin below CL's ~10 MiB limit. Transaction gas cap independently prevents single-transaction resource exhaustion.
